title: Salisbury screen: a 377-ohm sheet a quarter wave above a metal plane
source: F. Costa, A. Monorchio, G. Manara, IEEE EMC Magazine 5(2), 67-74 (2016), Fig. 5(a) and Table 1
notes: Costa gives a 5 mm air spacer on a ground plane, and states 377 ohm/sq for a Salisbury screen in general but not for Fig. 5(a) itself; 377 is assumed. The ground plane is copper (5.8e7 S/m, 0.1 mm thick: many skin depths). The sheet is a 1 um layer of the resistive_sheet model. For a perfect conductor and an infinitely thin sheet, R = c^2 / (4 + c^2) with c = cot(k0 d): the test checks that to 1e-3. Costa's Table 1 gives a -15 dB fractional bandwidth of 45.4%; the ideal formula gives 44.2%, which suggests a sheet resistance other than 377 for that figure.
